items.title: aioddp
items.text:
aioddp is a standalone, platform-agnostic asyncio library for sending DDP (Distributed Display Protocol) pixel data to LED controllers, with a small deterministic effect library and a bench-test CLI. The core package has no runtime dependencies.

Status

Pre-release. Interfaces may change before 0.1.0. Formerly named pyddp; renamed because the pyddp name on PyPI belongs to an unrelated project.

Guide CLI Bench-test new hardware: query, walk a pixel, fill, run effects. Guide Effects The six deterministic effects, their params, and the EffectRunner. Reference Controller compatibility Tested controllers and how to test yours. Reference API reference Sender, strip and segments, effects, discovery — generated from docstrings.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• DDP v1 sender: header encode, frame chunking, push flag, sequence numbers
  • Segments mapped to byte offsets, so parts of one string can be driven separately
  • RGB and RGBW, configurable color order and data type byte
  • Six deterministic effects and an EffectRunner
  • Global brightness cap enforced in the library; callers can lower it but not bypass it
  • Bench-test CLI for hardware bring-up

items.title: Installation
items.text:
pip install aioddp
pip install "aioddp[cli]"   # adds the aioddp command

Requires Python 3.12+.

items.title: Quick start
items.text:
import asyncio
from aioddp import DDPSender, EffectRunner, Segment, Strip


async def main():
    strip = Strip(host="10.0.40.20", pixel_count=300, brightness_cap=0.6)
    roof = Segment("roofline", start=0, length=260)
    peak = Segment("peak", start=260, length=40)

    async with DDPSender(strip) as tx:
        await tx.fill(roof, rgb=(255, 140, 40), brightness=0.6)
        runner = EffectRunner(tx, peak, effect="chase", fps=30, params={"speed": 1.0})
        await runner.start()
        await asyncio.sleep(10)
        await runner.stop()


asyncio.run(main())

Host and pixel counts are placeholders.

items.title: Layout discovery
items.text:
Controllers that answer the DDP JSON config query describe their own outputs:

from aioddp import Strip, discover

layout = await discover("10.0.40.20")
if layout:
    strip = Strip(host=layout.host, pixel_count=layout.pixel_count, data_type=layout.data_type)
    segments = layout.segments()  # one per active controller output

Controllers that serve their layout over HTTP (the Minleon NDB-Pro) are read by the separate pyminleon library, which can pass the document to aioddp.parse_config.

items.title: Controller compatibility
items.text: DDP receivers differ in what they accept and how they behave when data stops. This page records what has been tested with aioddp. Nothing is claimed that has not been run on hardware.

items.title: Minleon NDB-Pro notes
items.text:
• Layout discovery. It does not answer DDP queries to destination 250 or 251, whether the query comes from an ephemeral source port or from port 4048, so aioddp query gets no answer. It serves the DDP JSON config document over plain HTTP instead; reading that, and controlling its built-in effects, is the job of the separate pyminleon library. Its document parses with aioddp.parse_config.
  • Offsets. Every output has a ss starting slot, 1-based, in one flat channel buffer. With "RGB=>RGBW" conversion the sender sends 3 channels per pixel and output 2 of an 80-pixel output 1 starts at slot 241, pixel 80. Outputs can be auto-filled contiguously or placed by hand, so read the slots rather than assuming they are contiguous.
  • Reverse. The per-output "Reverse?" setting is applied by the controller. aioddp query reports it and leaves segment reverse off so the two do not cancel.
  • Status document. Reports manufacturer 3WL, model NDBPRO, firmware, MAC, "push": true, input voltage, current, and fuse state.
  • DDP and built-in effects. DDP data overrides the running built-in effect immediately. About 20 s after DDP stops, the controller falls back to its built-in effect; this was measured with the status document's current readback, not by eye. So holding a DDP frame needs keepalive_interval, and handing the lights back to the controller means stopping DDP: DDPSender.release() pauses keepalive until the next frame.
  • Built-in effect control. Selecting built-in effects, intensity, and stored presets is HTTP, not DDP, and lives in pyminleon. aioddp only provides DDPSender.release() to stop DDP so the controller can fall back.

Reports for other controllers are welcome: open a Controller Compatibility Report.

items.title: How to test a controller
items.text:
Install the CLI (pip install "aioddp[cli]") and use a short string. Replace HOST and N with the controller address and pixel count. The CLI defaults to a brightness cap of 1.0; pass --cap 0.5 if the string is not power-injected.

  1. Layout. aioddp --host HOST query asks for the controller's outputs over DDP. If it answers, it prints the pixel count, one line per output, and a config.yaml to paste; record whether it answered.
  2. Count and order. aioddp --host HOST --count N test runs an order check (red, green, blue, white on RGBW), walks one pixel down the string, then lights both ends. If colors do not match the labels, fix --order. Where the walk stops is the real pixel count; a jump or stall marks an output boundary.
  3. Data type byte. Run aioddp --host HOST --count N --data-type-byte 1 fill --color ff0000, then the same with --data-type-byte 0. Compare against the default (0x0B for RGB, 0x1B for RGBW with --type rgbw). Record which values light the string.
  4. Flat buffer or per-output offsets. On a multi-output controller where each output has fewer than 500 pixels, run aioddp --host HOST --count N --segment 500:10 fill --color ff0000. Lit pixels on a later output mean one flat buffer; nothing lit (or output 1 lit) means per-output offsets.
  5. Behavior when DDP stops. Run aioddp --host HOST --count N fill --color ff8800, then stop sending and time how long until the controller holds, blanks, or falls back to built-in effects. This decides whether keepalive is needed.
  6. Gamma. Run aioddp --host HOST --count N --no-gamma fill --color 808080, then --gamma 2.2 with the same color. The one that looks like half brightness tells you whether the controller already applies gamma.
  7. Zero-length push latch. Send two segments with push=False from the library, then a zero-length push, and see whether the frame latches. This needs a short script against DDPSender (the CLI always pushes).

Record the results in a Controller Compatibility Report, including model, firmware, pixel type, outputs used, and aioddp version.

items.title: aioddp.discovery
items.text:
Read a controller's output layout from the DDP JSON config query, or parse a config document fetched elsewhere.

items.title: fade
items.text:
async def fade(sender: DDPSender,
               segment: Segment,
               start: bytes,
               end: bytes,
               *,
               duration: float,
               fps: int = DEFAULT_FPS,
               brightness: float = 1.0) -> None

Linearly interpolate segment from start to end over duration seconds.

Sends max(1, round(duration * fps)) frames on an anchored schedule, frame i of n at i * duration / n, so the last, exactly end, lands at duration. duration <= 0 sends end once. Cancelling leaves the last sent frame on the wire.

items.title: CLI
items.text:
The aioddp command is a bench-test tool for bringing up new hardware. Install it with the cli extra:

pip install "aioddp[cli]"

items.title: Commands
items.text:
aioddp --host 10.0.40.20 query                           # ask the controller for its outputs; prints a config.yaml
aioddp --host 10.0.40.20 --count 300 test                # walk a lit pixel down the string
aioddp --host 10.0.40.20 --count 300 fill --color ff8800 --brightness 0.5
aioddp --host 10.0.40.20 --count 300 effect chase --param speed=8
aioddp --host 10.0.40.20 --count 300 off
aioddp effects                                           # list effects and params

Run aioddp query first against new hardware, then aioddp test. query uses the DDP JSON config query; a controller that does not answer it is configured by hand. Host and count can also come from config.yaml (the format query prints).

Host and pixel counts above are placeholders.

items.title: Effects
items.text:
Effects are pure functions of segment length, time, params, and seed, so a frame is reproducible. twinkle uses the seed; the others ignore it. Run one on a segment with EffectRunner, or from the CLI with aioddp effect <name>.

Effect Params solid (static) color breathe color, period, min_level chase colors, speed, spacing, width, background twinkle base_color, sparkle_color, density, speed rainbow speed, spread, saturation palette (static) colors, block_size

aioddp effects lists every effect with its params and defaults.

items.title: Render budget
items.text: Every effect renders 500 pixels with a median under 2 ms, enforced by the test suite, so a 30 fps runner leaves the event loop almost entirely free.

items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Module: cli.py, installed as aioddp via the [cli] extra (click, rich, pyyaml)

items.title: Scope
items.text: Bench tool for a controller with no Home Assistant in the loop. It is the first thing run against new hardware and the thing used to answer the design doc's open questions about the NDB-Pro. It is a thin shell over the library: no protocol or color logic lives here, and every command resolves to a Strip, an optional Segment, and one or two library calls inside asyncio.run.

items.text: aioddp [GLOBAL OPTIONS] COMMAND [ARGS]

items.title: Global options
items.text:
Option Default Notes --config PATH ./config.yaml if it exists YAML, see below. Missing file is fine unless --config was given explicitly --host HOST from config Required somewhere for every command but effects and version --count N from config Pixel count; required for every command that sends pixels, not for query --port N 4048 --type rgb\|rgbw rgb --order ORDER RGB, or RGBW with --type rgbw Color order string --cap FLOAT 1.0 Brightness cap. The CLI defaults to 1.0 because the bench user is standing next to the lights; hass-ddp defaults to 0.6 --gamma FLOAT / --no-gamma 2.2 --data-type-byte INT unset Override the wire byte; used to test whether a controller cares --segment NAME whole strip A segment from config, or START:LENGTH[:r] ad hoc, e.g. 260:40:r -v / -vv INFO / DEBUG logging to stderr. DEBUG prints one line per packet: sequence, offset, length, push --json Machine-readable output where a command prints anything

Command-line values override config values; config values override library defaults. The merged Strip is built once in a click context object and validation errors print the ConfigError message and exit 1.

items.title: config.yaml
items.text:
strip:
  host: 10.0.40.20
  pixel_count: 300
  port: 4048
  data_type: rgb
  color_order: GRB
  brightness_cap: 0.6
  gamma: 2.2
segments:
  roofline: { start: 0, length: 260 }
  peak: { start: 260, length: 40, reverse: true }

Gitignored. Unknown keys are an error so a typo does not silently fall back to a default.

items.title: fill
items.text:
aioddp fill --color ff8800 [--brightness 1.0] [--segment NAME]

One fill, then exit. --color accepts anything parse_color does, plus --kelvin N as an alternative to --color.

items.title: off
items.text:
aioddp off [--segment NAME]

One off, exit.

items.title: effect
items.text:
aioddp effect NAME [--fps 30] [--param key=value ...] [--brightness 1.0] [--seed N] [--segment NAME] [--duration SECONDS] [--keep]

Runs an EffectRunner until Ctrl-C or --duration. On exit the segment is blanked unless --keep; a bench session that leaves the roof lit after Ctrl-C is a surprise, so blanking is the default here even though the library never blanks on its own. Static effects send once and exit immediately (and are not blanked, since the point was to leave them up). Params are validated before the socket opens; errors list the effect's params and defaults. Ctrl-C is handled by cancelling the runner and awaiting it, so the exit is clean and the final off always goes out.

A rich status line shows frames rendered, dropped, packets, send errors, and max render time, refreshed twice a second. Suppressed under --json, in which case a single JSON stats object prints on exit.

items.title: test
items.text:
aioddp test [--delay 0.05] [--hold 3] [--color ffffff] [--segment NAME] [--loop]

The hardware bring-up command. Phases, each announced on stderr:

  1. Order check: pixel 0 red, pixel 1 green, pixel 2 blue, pixel 3 white (RGBW only, on the W channel) for --hold seconds (default 3). The operator confirms the colors match the labels; if not, --order is wrong
  2. Walk: one pixel in --color walks from the first to the last pixel of the target at --delay seconds per step, printing the index as it goes. Where it stops is the real pixel count, and where it jumps or stalls is a wiring or output boundary
  3. Ends: first and last pixel lit together for --hold seconds, then off

--loop repeats phase 2 until Ctrl-C. Exit blanks the target.

items.title: query
items.text:
aioddp --host HOST query [--timeout 1.0] [--json]

Asks the controller for its layout: a DDP query to the JSON config and status destinations (no HTTP; controllers that only serve the document over HTTP are read by pyminleon). Prints the controller identity, one row per active output (pixels, start pixel, whether the controller reverses it), the total, and a config.yaml snippet with one segment per output. Needs no --count; it is how you find one. No answer exits 2. Details in 2026-10-29-aioddp-discovery.md.

items.title: effects
items.text:
aioddp effects [--json]

Table of effect name, static flag, description, and each param with kind, default, and range. --json emits the list_effects() structure. Needs no host.

items.title: version
items.text: Prints aioddp <version> from importlib.metadata.

items.title: Exit codes
items.text:
Code Meaning 0 Done 1 ConfigError, EffectError, DDPQueryError, usage error (click's default of 2 is remapped), bad config file 2 DDPSendError (could not open the socket or resolve the host); query with no answer 130 Ctrl-C (after clean shutdown)

Tracebacks never print without -vv.

items.title: Structure
items.text: cli.py is one module: a click group, a _build_strip(ctx) helper, a _resolve_segment(ctx, strip, name) helper, one function per command, and main(). Each command body is a small async def _run(...) executed with asyncio.run. Importing aioddp.cli without the extra installed raises ImportError with an install hint; aioddp itself never imports cli.

items.title: Tests (tests/test_cli.py)
items.text:
Through click.testing.CliRunner with the udp_listener fixture as the host and --port pointed at it. Parametrized where cases are variations of one behavior.

  • fill, off: packet on the wire with expected bytes; --segment from config and ad hoc START:LENGTH:r forms
  • Config precedence: config value, overridden by flag; unknown config key exits 1 with the key named
  • Missing host exits 1 with a usage message; unresolvable host exits 2
  • effect chase --duration 0.2: packets received, exit 0, final packet is zeros (blank on exit); with --keep the final packet is not zeros; a static effect sends one frame
  • effect with a bad param exits 1 and the message names the param
  • test --delay 0.001 on 5 pixels: order phase packets then 5 walk packets then the ends frame then blank
  • effects --json round-trips through json.loads and lists all six
  • query with host only against the listener's responder; --json; no answer exits 2; unusable-layout warnings
  • version prints the metadata version

items.title: aioddp component spec: color pipeline
items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Module: color.py

items.title: Scope
items.text: Pure functions that turn canonical pixel bytes into wire bytes for one strip, plus color helpers (Kelvin, hex, HSV). No I/O, no asyncio. Coverage target 95%+. This module is the single enforcement point for the brightness cap: DDPSender has no public path to the socket that skips process_frame.

items.title: Canonical pixel bytes
items.text:
Every producer (effects, fill, hass-ddp, the CLI) hands the sender a bytes of length * channels where:

  • Channel order is canonical: R, G, B, then W for RGBW strips
  • Values are 0 to 255, linear intent (what the caller wants to see, before gamma)
  • Pixel 0 is the first pixel of the segment in logical order; reverse is the strip's problem

Effects always render 3 channels. expand_rgb_to_rgbw inserts W = 0 after every triplet when the strip is RGBW. White on RGBW strips is only lit by explicit RGBW colors passed to fill or by a future RGBW-aware effect.

items.title: process_frame
items.text:
def process_frame(
    pixels: bytes,
    strip: Strip,
    *,
    brightness: float = 1.0,
    reverse: bool = False,
) -> bytes

Stages, in order:

  1. Validate: len(pixels) % strip.channels == 0 and 0.0 <= brightness <= 1.0, else ConfigError
  2. Level LUT: one 256-entry table applies per-call brightness, gamma, and the cap in one bytes.translate. Entry v is round(255 * cap * ((v / 255) * brightness) ** gamma), with gamma 1.0 when the strip disables it
  3. Reorder: if strip.color_order is canonical, skip. Otherwise build the output with per-channel strided slices using strip.channel_map (out[k::ch] = src[channel_map[k]::ch])
  4. Reverse: if reverse, reverse pixel order with per-channel strided slices (out[k::ch] = src[k::ch][::-1])

Brightness is applied before gamma so dimming is perceptual; the cap is applied after gamma so it bounds actual drive current, which is what protects a long run from brownout. The W channel goes through the same LUT.

items.title: LUT cache
items.text: _level_lut(brightness: float, gamma: float, cap: float) -> bytes is wrapped in functools.lru_cache(maxsize=256). Callers that sweep brightness (breathe, fades) hit distinct keys; 256 entries at 256 bytes each is 64 KB and covers every integer percent at one gamma and cap. Brightness is rounded to 4 decimals before lookup so float noise does not defeat the cache.

items.title: Performance
items.text: All four stages are C-speed (translate, slice assignment). 1000 RGBW pixels process in well under 100 µs. This is what leaves the effect's own render loop as the only Python-speed work per frame.

items.title: Color helpers
items.text:
RGB = tuple[int, int, int]
RGBW = tuple[int, int, int, int]
Color = RGB | RGBW

def parse_color(value: str | Sequence[int]) -> Color
def scale_color(color: Color, factor: float) -> Color
def lerp_color(a: Color, b: Color, t: float) -> Color
def kelvin_to_rgb(kelvin: int) -> RGB
def hsv_to_rgb(h: float, s: float, v: float) -> RGB
def solid_pixels(color: Color, length: int, channels: int) -> bytes
def expand_rgb_to_rgbw(pixels: bytes) -> bytes
  • parse_color accepts "ff8800", "#ff8800", "ff8800ff" (RGBW), a 3- or 4-tuple of ints, or a named color from a small table (red, green, blue, white, warmwhite, off). Anything else is ConfigError. Named colors exist for the CLI; the table is short and documented
  • solid_pixels pads an RGB color with W=0 on a 4-channel strip and raises ConfigError for an RGBW color on a 3-channel strip
  • kelvin_to_rgb is the Tanner Helland approximation. Input is clamped to 1000 to 40000; the documented supported range is 2000 to 6500 K and the docs say it is an approximation on RGB pixels. On RGBW strips the result goes into RGB with W=0; using the white channel for color temperature is a later feature
  • hsv_to_rgb is colorsys.hsv_to_rgb scaled to 0 to 255 and rounded. The rainbow effect uses a precomputed 1536-entry hue table rather than calling this per pixel

items.title: Summary
items.text:
aioddp is a standalone, platform-agnostic, asyncio Python library that sends DDP (Distributed Display Protocol) pixel data to LED controllers and renders effects as pure functions. It is the protocol half of a pydmp / hass-dmp style pair: hass-ddp imports it and contains no protocol code. If bytes are being built anywhere else, that code belongs here.

First target is a Minleon NDB-Pro driving Rainmin RGB+ pixels on a roofline, but aioddp knows no vendor and has no HTTP client. Vendor control (the NDB-Pro's built-in effects, its HTTP-served layout) lives in the separate pyminleon library.

items.title: What this is NOT
items.text:
• Not a Home Assistant integration (hass-ddp is)
  • Not a DDP receiver
  • Not an E1.31, Art-Net, or DMX sender
  • Not an xLights sequence player
  • Not audio-reactive
  • Not a WLED effect-library rewrite

items.title: Goals
items.text:
• Correct DDP v1 sender: header encode, frame chunking, push flag, sequence numbers
  • Segments mapped to byte offsets so independent parts of one string can be driven separately
  • A small, deterministic effect library
  • Global brightness cap enforced in the library so no caller can bypass it
  • CLI for bench testing a controller with no Home Assistant in the loop
  • Zero runtime dependencies for the core package

items.title: DDP protocol summary
items.text:
UDP to port 4048. A 10-byte header followed by raw pixel bytes. A frame larger than one packet is split by byte offset; the push flag on the last packet tells the receiver to latch the frame.

Bytes Field What we send 0 Flags Version 1 (0x40), plus push (0x01) on the last packet of a frame. Query (0x02) only on a layout read; never timecode or storage 1 Sequence Low 4 bits, cycling 1 to 15; 0 means unused 2 Data type 0x0B for 8-bit RGB, 0x1B for 8-bit RGBW. Configurable, since some receivers expect legacy 0x01 or ignore the field 3 Destination ID 1 (default output device) 4 to 7 Data offset Byte offset into the receiver's buffer, big-endian 8 to 9 Data length Payload bytes in this packet, big-endian 10+ Data Pixel bytes in the configured channel order
  • Max payload per packet: 1440 bytes (480 RGB pixels, 360 RGBW). Larger frames go out as several packets with increasing offsets, push set only on the last.
  • No priority, no acknowledgement. Two senders on one controller fight; only one source talks at a time.
  • Segments are byte ranges. A segment can be sent as its own packet(s) at its own offset without merging frames. To latch several segments together, send them without push and push once at the end.
  • The protocol's optional read side (query flag to destination 250 for JSON config, 251 for JSON status) is the only way to learn a controller's layout. It is supported, best effort, and some controllers publish the same JSON over HTTP instead; fetching that is out of scope here (pyminleon does it and passes the JSON to parse_config); see the discovery spec.

items.title: Core classes
items.text:
• Strip(host, pixel_count, port=4048, data_type=RGB, color_order="RGB", brightness_cap=1.0)
  • Segment(name, start, length, reverse=False): validated against the strip (no overlap required, but out-of-range is an error)
  • DDPSender(strip, keepalive_interval=None): async context manager. send_frame(pixels, segment=None, brightness=1.0, push=True), fill(segment, color, brightness), off(segment), push(), close(). Owns the sequence counter, a shadow buffer of the last wire bytes, and the optional keepalive task. There is no raw-bytes send: send_frame takes canonical RGB(W) pixels and always runs the color pipeline, which is how the cap is enforced
  • EffectRunner(sender, segment, effect, fps=30, params=None, brightness=1.0, seed=None): start(), stop(), update(params=, brightness=, fps=), wait(); cancels cleanly and never leaves an orphaned task. fade(sender, segment, start, end, duration) is the transition helper
  • Effect protocol: render(length: int, t: float, params: Mapping, seed: int) -> bytes returning length * 3 canonical RGB bytes, plus a declared params schema with defaults and a static flag
  • discover(host): ControllerLayout (pixel count, one OutputInfo per output, channels, identity) from a DDP query, or None; parse_config builds the same layout from a document fetched by other means; layout.segments() gives one Segment per active output. DDPSender.query(destination) is the underlying read

items.title: Public API sketch
items.text:
from aioddp import DDPSender, EffectRunner, Segment, Strip

strip = Strip(host="10.0.40.20", pixel_count=300, brightness_cap=0.6)
roof = Segment("roofline", start=0, length=260)
peak = Segment("peak", start=260, length=40)

async with DDPSender(strip) as tx:
    await tx.fill(roof, rgb=(255, 140, 40), brightness=0.6)
    runner = EffectRunner(tx, peak, effect="chase", fps=30, params={"speed": 1.0})
    await runner.start()

Host and pixel counts above are placeholders.

items.title: Color pipeline
items.text:
Every frame, from any caller, goes through the same stage before it hits the socket:

  1. Effect or fill produces linear RGB(W) per pixel
  2. Per-call brightness applied
  3. Gamma correction (table, configurable, default 2.2; can be disabled if the controller already applies it)
  4. Global brightness cap applied
  5. Reorder to the strip's color order
  6. Optional segment reverse

The cap lives in step 4 and is not optional at the API level: callers can lower it, not skip it. This protects long runs without power injection from voltage drop and color shift.

Kelvin to RGB uses a standard approximation for 2000 to 6500 K. Color temp on RGB-only pixels is an approximation and the docs say so.

items.title: Effects (v1)
items.text:
Each effect is a pure function of segment length, time, and params, deterministic given a seed so tests can assert exact bytes.

Effect Params Solid color. Not a loop: render once, send, keepalive only if enabled Breathe color, period Chase / theater chase colors, speed, spacing Twinkle base color, sparkle color, density, seed Rainbow speed, spread Palette fill list of colors, block size (static; holiday, team colors)

Effects must render a few hundred pixels in well under 1 ms. A benchmark test enforces a budget so hass-ddp can run them on the HA event loop without stalling it.

items.title: Sender behavior
items.text:
• asyncio datagram endpoint, no threads
  • Sequence counter cycles 1 to 15 per sender
  • Frame chunking at 1440 bytes, push on the last packet only
  • Optional keepalive: resend the last full frame every N seconds when nothing else has been sent. Off by default; enabled only if the controller blanks without data
  • close() stops keepalive and closes the socket. It does not blank the lights; blanking is an explicit off()
  • Send errors raise DDPSendError; transient OSError on UDP send is logged and counted, not fatal, so one dropped packet never kills an effect

items.title: CLI
items.text:
Installed via the [cli] extra (click, rich, pyyaml), same pattern as pydmp. Optional config.yaml (gitignored) for host and pixel count.

  • aioddp fill <host> --count N --color ff8800 [--brightness 0.5] [--cap 0.6]
  • aioddp effect <host> --count N --effect chase --fps 30 [--param speed=1.0]
  • aioddp off <host> --count N
  • aioddp test <host> --count N: walks a single lit pixel down the string to confirm pixel count, channel order, and segment boundaries. First thing to run against real hardware
  • aioddp query <host>: asks the controller for its output layout and prints a ready-to-paste config.yaml; run it before test on a controller that answers
  • aioddp effects: list effects and their params

items.title: Error handling and logging
items.text:
• Exception hierarchy rooted at DDPError: ConfigError, DDPSendError, EffectError, DDPQueryError
  • Input validation: pixel count > 0, segments in range, brightness and cap in 0.0 to 1.0, fps in 1 to 60, data type in the supported set
  • Standard logging; never log full frames above DEBUG

items.title: Testing
items.text:
• pytest + pytest-asyncio (asyncio_mode = "auto"), pytest-cov
  • Golden-byte tests for header encoding, chunking, offsets, push flag, sequence wrap
  • Local UDP listener fixture to assert exactly what the sender puts on the wire
  • Effects tested as pure functions with fixed seeds, no network
  • Render-time budget test per effect
  • Coverage target 80%+ overall, 95%+ on protocol.py and color.py

items.title: Repo conventions (mirror pydmp)
items.text:
• src/aioddp layout, hatchling build backend
  • requires-python = ">=3.12", Apache-2.0 license, author Anthony Mattas
  • dependencies = []; dev, cli, docs extras with exact pins
  • ruff lint and format (line length 120, rules E, F, I, B, UP, SIM, S, S101 ignored in tests), mypy strict pinned to 3.12, bandit, pre-commit
  • .editorconfig, .gitignore copied from pydmp (adds config.yaml)
  • CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md at the root, same structure as pydmp's
  • Docs: Zensical + mike, published to https://amattas.github.io/aioddp/, API reference generated with pydoc-markdown, scripts/publish_versioned_docs.py copied from pydmp
  • GitHub: ci.yml, docs.yml, release.yml manual-only; release from an X.Y.Z tag on main, PyPI trusted publishing via the pypi environment with a reviewer gate. CODEOWNERS, dependabot.yml, issue templates (swap panel_compatibility for controller_compatibility)
  • docs/compatibility.md lists controllers tested and what data type byte and timeout behavior each one has

items.title: Milestones
items.text:
1. Core: protocol, sender, color pipeline with cap, fill, off, test CLI. Done when the CLI lights the real string at the right count and order
  2. Effects: registry, six v1 effects, EffectRunner, effect CLI, budget tests
  3. Release 0.1.0: docs site, PyPI publish, compatibility page with the NDB-Pro

Maintenance-only after 0.1.0 until school is done.

items.title: Open questions
items.text:
• Is aioddp free on PyPI? If not, pick a name before scaffolding
  • Does the NDB-Pro honor the data type byte, or accept anything?
  • Does the NDB-Pro treat DDP offsets as one flat buffer across its 8 outputs, or per output? One flat buffer: each output has a 1-based starting slot in its config document (output 2 at slot 241 after 80 three-channel pixels on output 1). Answered 2026-10-29 by aioddp query; see docs/compatibility.md
  • Can the layout be discovered? Not over DDP on the NDB-Pro (no reply to queries), but it serves the DDP JSON config document over HTTP, which pyminleon reads and hands to parse_config; discover() is the DDP query alone
  • What does the NDB-Pro do when DDP stops: hold, blank, or fall back to built-in effects, and after how long? Decides the keepalive default
  • Does the NDB-Pro apply its own gamma? Decides whether ours is on by default
  • Is a sync wrapper worth it (pydmp has one), or is the CLI enough for scripting? The sender spec recommends dropping it from 0.1.0; sender_sync.py is out of the tree until someone asks

The remaining hardware questions are answered by the checklist at the end of the testing spec and recorded in docs/compatibility.md.

items.title: aioddp component spec: effects
items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Package: effects/ (__init__.py, base.py, solid.py, breathe.py, chase.py, twinkle.py, rainbow.py, palette.py)

items.title: Scope
items.text: Six deterministic effects, a parameter schema, and a registry. Effects know nothing about strips, sockets, gamma, or the cap: they produce canonical RGB bytes for a segment length at a time t. The runner (next spec) owns timing.

items.title: Effect contract (base.py)
items.text:
class ParamSpec(NamedTuple):
    kind: Literal["float", "int", "bool", "color", "colors"]
    default: Any
    description: str
    min: float | None = None
    max: float | None = None

class Effect(Protocol):
    name: ClassVar[str]
    description: ClassVar[str]
    params: ClassVar[Mapping[str, ParamSpec]]
    static: ClassVar[bool]            # True: render once, no loop

    def render(self, length: int, t: float, params: Mapping[str, Any], seed: int) -> bytes

Rules every effect follows, enforced by the shared parametrized test:

  • Pure: render output depends only on (length, t, params, seed). No instance state that changes between calls. Internal caches keyed on those inputs are fine and expected (per-pixel phases, hue tables)
  • Output: exactly length * 3 bytes, canonical RGB. Effects never render W; the sender expands for RGBW strips
  • Time: t is seconds since the runner started, non-negative, unbounded. Effects use modular arithmetic so t = 1e6 renders the same as t % period
  • Budget: 500 pixels in under 2 ms median on the CI runner (see testing spec). Per-pixel Python loops are allowed; per-pixel function calls and tuple allocation are what blow the budget, so effects build a bytearray and write channels directly
  • Params: render receives already-validated, default-merged params. It never looks up defaults itself

items.title: Parameter validation
items.text:
def validate_params(effect: type[Effect], params: Mapping[str, Any] | None) -> dict[str, Any]

Merges defaults, rejects unknown keys, coerces and range-checks by kind. color accepts anything parse_color does and normalizes to an RGB tuple (RGBW input is rejected with EffectError since effects render RGB). colors is a non-empty list of the same. int and float are range-checked against min/max when set; bool accepts bool only. Failures raise EffectError naming the param. The CLI's --param key=value strings go through this with string coercion for numbers ("1.5", "3", "true") and comma-split hex lists for colors.

items.title: Registry (effects/__init__.py)
items.text:
EFFECTS: Mapping[str, type[Effect]]   # explicit dict, no import-time magic
def get_effect(name: str) -> type[Effect]      # EffectError on unknown name, message lists valid names
def list_effects() -> list[EffectInfo]         # name, description, static, params, color_param; used by CLI and hass-ddp effect_list

color_param names the one parameter a single user-picked color drives (BaseEffect defaults it to None; effects that do not subclass it are read with getattr, so the Effect protocol does not require it). EffectInfo.color_params(rgb) returns the params that apply that color: {color_param: rgb} for a color param, {color_param: [rgb]} for a colors param, {} when there is none. hass-ddp uses it to map Home Assistant's rgb_color onto whatever effect is running, so the integration holds no per-effect knowledge.

Effect color_param solid, breathe color chase colors twinkle sparkle_color rainbow, palette none

Names are lowercase ASCII: solid, breathe, chase, twinkle, rainbow, palette. hass-ddp uses these strings verbatim as the HA effect values, so renaming one is a breaking change.

items.title: The six effects
items.text: Colors below are RGB tuples. Defaults are chosen to look right on a roofline at 30 fps without tuning.

items.title: solid (static)
items.text:
Param Kind Default color color (255, 255, 255)

render ignores t and seed. Exists so "effect = solid" and "no effect" are the same thing in hass-ddp.

items.title: breathe
items.text:
Param Kind Default Range color color (255, 255, 255) period float 4.0 0.5 to 60 min_level float 0.05 0.0 to 1.0

level = min_level + (1 - min_level) * (0.5 - 0.5 * cos(2π t / period)). Whole segment is scale_color(color, level). One scale_color call per frame, then bytes * length; this is the cheapest effect.

items.title: chase (theater chase)
items.text:
Param Kind Default Range colors colors [(255, 255, 255)] speed float 8.0 -100 to 100, pixels per second; negative runs backwards spacing int 3 2 to 50 width int 1 1 to spacing background color (0, 0, 0)

shift = floor(t * speed) mod (spacing * len(colors)). Wrapping at the full color cycle rather than at spacing keeps multi-color blocks moving instead of snapping back every spacing steps; the lit pattern is the same either way. Pixel i is lit when (i - shift) mod spacing < width. A lit pixel's color is colors[((i - shift) // spacing) mod len(colors)] so multi-color chases keep their color blocks moving with the chase. Unlit pixels get background. width > spacing is a validation error (checked in validate_params as a cross-param rule).

items.title: twinkle
items.text:
Param Kind Default Range base_color color (0, 0, 0) sparkle_color color (255, 255, 255) density float 0.15 0.0 to 1.0, fraction of pixels that twinkle speed float 1.0 0.05 to 10, twinkle cycles per second

Per (length, seed) the effect computes and caches, with random.Random(seed), a phase φ_i ∈ [0, 1) and a selection value s_i ∈ [0, 1) for each pixel. Pixel i twinkles when s_i < density; its level is a triangle wave tri((t * speed + φ_i) mod 1) rising 0 to 1 to 0, and its color is lerp_color(base, sparkle, level). Non-twinkling pixels are base_color. Cache: functools.lru_cache(maxsize=32) on a module function _tables(length, seed). Changing density or speed through update does not change which pixels could twinkle, only how many of the pre-rolled ones do, which keeps updates visually continuous.

items.title: rainbow
items.text:
Param Kind Default Range speed float 0.1 -5 to 5, hue rotations per second spread float 1.0 0.01 to 20, hue cycles across the segment saturation float 1.0 0.0 to 1.0

hue_i = (i / length * spread + t * speed) mod 1. RGB comes from a module-level 1536-entry hue wheel built once at import (hsv_to_rgb(h, 1, 1) sampled); saturation below 1.0 lerps toward white per pixel. Index math is integer: idx = int(hue_i * 1536).

items.title: palette (static)
items.text:
Param Kind Default Range colors colors [(255, 0, 0), (0, 255, 0)] block_size int 1 1 to 1000

Pixel i is colors[(i // block_size) mod len(colors)]. Holiday and team-color fills. Static, so the runner sends it once.

items.title: Determinism
items.text: seed defaults to 0 in the runner when the caller passes None, so two runners with the same inputs produce identical frames. Only twinkle consumes the seed in v1; the others accept and ignore it. Tests render every effect at t in {0, 0.5, 123456.789} with a fixed seed and compare against golden bytes checked into tests/golden/<effect>_<t>.bin plus a .json sidecar with the effect, length (300), t, seed, and merged params. Regenerating goldens is an explicit python -m tests.golden --write step, never automatic.

items.title: Tests (tests/test_effects.py)
items.text:
One parametrized test over EFFECTS.values() for each contract rule:

  • Output length is length * 3 for lengths 1, 2, 300
  • Same inputs twice give identical bytes; different seeds differ only for twinkle
  • t and t + 10_000 * period_equivalent match within one frame's rounding (periodicity)
  • Golden bytes for default params at three t values
  • validate_params: defaults fill in, unknown key rejected, each kind's bad value rejected, width > spacing rejected, CLI string coercion works
  • Budget: median of 50 renders at 500 pixels under the threshold in the testing spec

Effect-specific tests are few: chase pixel pattern at t=0 and after one shift, breathe level at t=0 and t=period/2, twinkle density produces roughly density * length twinkling pixels at seed 0 (asserted within ±30%), rainbow pixel 0 at t=0 is red, palette block boundaries.

items.title: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions
items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Modules: const.py, exceptions.py, protocol.py
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: Scope
items.text: Everything that turns pixel bytes into DDP packets. No sockets, no color math. protocol.py is pure, synchronous, and has no imports beyond struct, dataclasses, enum, and collections.abc. Coverage target 95%+.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: const.py
items.text:
DDP_PORT = 4048
HEADER_SIZE = 10
MAX_DATA_LEN = 1440  # DDP recommended max payload; 480 RGB or 360 RGBW pixels
MAX_OFFSET = 0xFFFF_FFFF  # 32-bit data offset
HEADER_FORMAT = ">BBBBIH"  # flags, sequence, data type, destination, offset, length

FLAG_VERSION_MASK = 0xC0
FLAG_VERSION_1 = 0x40
FLAG_TIMECODE = 0x10
FLAG_STORAGE = 0x08
FLAG_REPLY = 0x04
FLAG_QUERY = 0x02
FLAG_PUSH = 0x01

SEQUENCE_MIN = 1
SEQUENCE_MAX = 15  # low 4 bits; 0 means "sequence unused"

DESTINATION_DEFAULT = 1  # default output device
DESTINATION_ALL = 255
DESTINATION_CONTROL = 246  # JSON control
DESTINATION_CONFIG = 250  # JSON config, read by query
DESTINATION_STATUS = 251  # JSON status, read by query

DEFAULT_FPS = 30
MAX_FPS = 60
DEFAULT_GAMMA = 2.2
DEFAULT_BRIGHTNESS_CAP = 1.0

The timecode and storage bits are named so the decoder can report them and tests can assert they are never set; the sender never sets them. The query bit is set only by build_query_packet, and the reply bit only ever arrives from a controller (see the discovery spec).
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: DataType
items.text:
class DataType(Enum):
    RGB = ("RGB", 3, 0x0B)  # type 001 (RGB), size 011 (8-bit)
    RGBW = ("RGBW", 4, 0x1B)  # type 011 (RGBW), size 011 (8-bit)

    @property
    def channels(self) -> int: ...
    @property
    def wire_byte(self) -> int: ...

The DDP data type byte is C R TTT SSS: bit 7 customer-defined, bit 6 reserved, bits 5 to 3 type (1 RGB, 2 HSL, 3 RGBW, 4 greyscale), bits 2 to 0 size (3 means 8 bits per channel). 0x0B and 0x1B follow from that. Only these two members exist; HSL and greyscale are out of scope.

DATA_TYPE_LEGACY = 0x01 is exported for receivers that expect what older senders put in this byte. The strip's data_type_byte override (see the strip spec) lets a user send 0x01, 0x00, or anything else while the library still knows the pixel has 3 or 4 channels. The wire byte never changes how the library lays out bytes; only DataType.channels does.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: exceptions.py
items.text:
class DDPError(Exception): ...


class ConfigError(DDPError, ValueError): ...  # bad strip, segment, params, or color


class DDPSendError(DDPError): ...  # socket could not be opened or sender is closed


class EffectError(DDPError): ...  # unknown effect, bad params, or render failure


class DDPQueryError(DDPError): ...  # a controller answered a query or config request with something unusable

ConfigError also subclasses ValueError so callers that validate user input generically still catch it. Transient UDP send errors are not exceptions (see the sender spec); DDPSendError is reserved for "this sender cannot send at all".
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: protocol.py
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: DDPHeader
items.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class DDPHeader:
    flags: int
    sequence: int
    data_type: int
    destination: int
    offset: int
    length: int

    @property
    def version(self) -> int        # (flags & FLAG_VERSION_MASK) >> 6
    @property
    def push(self) -> bool          # bool(flags & FLAG_PUSH)
    @property
    def query(self) -> bool         # bool(flags & FLAG_QUERY)
    @property
    def reply(self) -> bool         # bool(flags & FLAG_REPLY)

    def encode(self) -> bytes       # struct.pack(HEADER_FORMAT, ...)
    @classmethod
    def decode(cls, data: bytes) -> DDPHeader

encode validates nothing; the builders below produce valid values and the dataclass is the typed carrier. decode raises ValueError on fewer than 10 bytes. It exists for the test listener fixture, the CLI's debug dump, and the sender's reply matching; the library never receives pixel data.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: build_header
items.text:
def build_header(
    *,
    offset: int,
    length: int,
    sequence: int,
    data_type: int,
    push: bool,
    destination: int = DESTINATION_DEFAULT,
) -> bytes

Flags are always FLAG_VERSION_1, plus FLAG_PUSH when push. Raises ConfigError on offset > MAX_OFFSET, length > MAX_DATA_LEN, sequence outside 0 to 15, data_type or destination outside 0 to 255. Sequence 0 is allowed here (it means "unused") even though the sender never emits it.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: SequenceCounter
items.text:
class SequenceCounter:
    def __init__(self, start: int = SEQUENCE_MIN) -> None
    def next(self) -> int           # returns current, then advances; 15 wraps to 1
    @property
    def current(self) -> int

Increments once per packet, not once per frame, per the DDP spec. A 3-packet frame consumes three sequence numbers. start outside 1 to 15 raises ConfigError.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: chunk_data
items.text:
def chunk_data(data: bytes, base_offset: int = 0, max_len: int = MAX_DATA_LEN) -> list[tuple[int, bytes]]

Splits data into (offset, chunk) pairs of at most max_len bytes with offsets base_offset, base_offset + max_len, .... Empty data raises ConfigError (a zero-length frame has no meaning; an explicit latch uses build_push_packet). Does not care about pixel boundaries: a chunk may split a pixel because the receiver reassembles by byte offset. Tests cover a chunk boundary inside a pixel.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: build_packets
items.text:
def build_packets(
    data: bytes,
    *,
    base_offset: int,
    data_type: int,
    sequence: SequenceCounter,
    push: bool = True,
    destination: int = DESTINATION_DEFAULT,
    max_len: int = MAX_DATA_LEN,
) -> list[bytes]

Calls chunk_data, then build_header per chunk with push set only on the final chunk (and only if push is true), and returns complete packets (header + chunk). Pulls one sequence number per packet in order. The whole list is built before anything is sent so a validation error leaves the counter untouched; the counter is advanced only on success. Implementation: compute chunks, validate, then draw sequence numbers in one pass.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: build_push_packet
items.text:
def build_push_packet(*, sequence: SequenceCounter, data_type: int, destination: int = DESTINATION_DEFAULT) -> bytes

A header-only packet, length = 0, offset = 0, push set. Used to latch several segments sent with push=False. Whether a receiver honors a zero-length push is controller-dependent and is recorded per controller in docs/compatibility.md.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: build_query_packet
items.text:
def build_query_packet(*, sequence: SequenceCounter, destination: int, offset: int = 0, length: int = 0) -> bytes

A header-only read request: flags FLAG_VERSION_1 | FLAG_QUERY, data type 0, the given destination (normally DESTINATION_CONFIG or DESTINATION_STATUS), one sequence number consumed. Same range checks as build_header. The reply handling lives in the sender; see 2026-10-29-aioddp-discovery.md.
path: aioddp component spec: protocol, constants, exceptions

items.title: Golden vectors
items.text:
These are the byte-exact cases the protocol tests assert. Hex, spaces for readability.

Case Header RGB, seq 1, offset 0, len 3, push 41 01 0B 01 00000000 0003 RGB, seq 2, offset 1440, len 3, no push 40 02 0B 01 000005A0 0003 RGBW, seq 15, offset 0, len 4, push 41 0F 1B 01 00000000 0004 Legacy byte, seq 1, offset 0, len 3, push 41 01 01 01 00000000 0003 Push-only latch, seq 3, RGB 41 03 0B 01 00000000 0000 Query config, seq 1 42 01 00 FA 00000000 0000 Query status, seq 2 42 02 00 FB 00000000 0000

Chunking cases:

Input Packets 1440 bytes, offset 0 one packet, offset 0, len 1440, push 1441 bytes, offset 0 offset 0 len 1440 no push; offset 1440 len 1 push 3000 bytes, offset 600 offsets 600, 2040, 3480 with lens 1440, 1440, 120; push on the last only 900 bytes, offset 0, push=False one packet, no push

Sequence: 15 consecutive next() calls from a fresh counter return 1..15; the 16th returns 1. A 3-packet frame built from a counter at 14 gets 14, 15, 1.

items.title: Out of scope
items.text:
• Storage and timecode flags
  • Writing to destinations 246, 250, or 251 (JSON control and configuration writes); only reads are supported
  • Destination 254 (DMX transit)
  • Receiving pixel data

items.title: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades
items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Module: runner.py
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: Scope
items.text: The one place an asyncio task renders effects on a schedule. Also the fade helper hass-ddp uses for transition. Everything here is designed so that hass-ddp can start and stop runners on the HA event loop without ever leaking a task or stalling the loop.
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: EffectRunner
items.text:
class EffectRunner:
    def __init__(
        self,
        sender: DDPSender,
        segment: Segment,
        effect: str | type[Effect],
        *,
        fps: int = DEFAULT_FPS,
        params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None,
        brightness: float = 1.0,
        seed: int | None = None,
    ) -> None

    async def start(self) -> None
    async def stop(self) -> None
    def update(self, *, params: Mapping[str, Any] | None = None, brightness: float | None = None, fps: int | None = None) -> None
    async def wait(self) -> None               # returns when the task finishes (static effect done, stop, or error)

    @property
    def running(self) -> bool
    @property
    def error(self) -> BaseException | None
    @property
    def stats(self) -> RunnerStats

    async def __aenter__(self) -> EffectRunner  # start()
    async def __aexit__(...) -> None            # stop()
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: Construction
items.text:
• effect as a string is resolved through get_effect; unknown raises EffectError immediately, not at start()
  • params go through validate_params at construction, so a bad param fails before any task exists
  • fps is 1 <= fps <= MAX_FPS, brightness is 0.0 to 1.0, else ConfigError
  • seed of None becomes 0
  • The sender must be open at start(), not at construction; hass-ddp builds runners before the entry is fully up
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: The loop
items.text:
t0 = loop.time()
next_deadline = t0
frame = 0
while True:
    now = loop.time()
    t = now - t0
    pixels = effect.render(segment.length, t, params, seed)
    await sender.send_frame(pixels, segment=segment, brightness=brightness, push=True)
    frame += 1
    if effect.static: break
    next_deadline += 1 / fps
    if next_deadline < now:                 # fell behind by at least a frame
        dropped += int((now - next_deadline) * fps) + 1
        next_deadline = now + 1 / fps
    await asyncio.sleep(next_deadline - loop.time())
  • The schedule is anchored to t0, so jitter does not accumulate and t is wall-time true: an effect with period=4 really takes 4 s per cycle at any fps
  • When the loop falls behind, it resyncs rather than bursting catch-up frames
  • params, brightness, and fps are read fresh on every iteration from instance attributes; update() just assigns them, so it is synchronous, safe to call from any coroutine on the loop, and takes effect at the next frame. update(params=...) re-validates and replaces the whole mapping (merged with defaults), it does not patch keys. fps changes also reset next_deadline to now
  • Static effects render once, send, and the task exits with running false and no error. Persistence of a static frame is the keepalive's job
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: Cancellation and errors
items.text:
• start() creates the task with name aioddp-effect-<effect>-<segment>; calling it while running raises RuntimeError (programmer error, not a DDPError)
  • stop() cancels the task, awaits it, swallows only CancelledError, and is idempotent. After stop() returns there is no task. It does not blank the segment; hass-ddp decides whether to off() or fill() next
  • EffectError or any other exception from render is caught inside the task, logged at ERROR with the effect name and segment, stored in runner.error, and ends the loop. It is not re-raised into the loop's exception handler because nothing awaits the task in hass-ddp's normal flow. wait() re-raises it for callers that do
  • DDPSendError (sender closed underneath the runner) ends the loop the same way. Transient send errors never reach here; the sender counts them
  • The runner holds no reference cycle with the task; stop() or task completion clears self._task
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: RunnerStats
items.text:
@dataclass(slots=True)
class RunnerStats:
    frames_rendered: int = 0
    frames_dropped: int = 0
    last_render_seconds: float = 0.0  # wall time of the most recent render call
    max_render_seconds: float = 0.0

max_render_seconds is what hass-ddp diagnostics show when someone asks why HA is laggy.
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: fade
items.text:
async def fade(
    sender: DDPSender,
    segment: Segment,
    start: bytes,
    end: bytes,
    *,
    duration: float,
    fps: int = DEFAULT_FPS,
    brightness: float = 1.0,
) -> None

Linear interpolation from start to end (both canonical pixel bytes of the segment's length) over duration seconds, sending max(1, round(duration * fps)) frames on the same anchored schedule as the runner, frame i of n at t0 + i * duration / n, so the last frame, exactly end, lands at duration; a non-finite duration raises ConfigError. Interpolation is done with one bytes LUT-free loop per frame over bytearrays; at 300 pixels and 30 fps that is well inside budget. duration <= 0 sends end once. Cancelling the awaiting coroutine stops the fade mid-way with the last sent frame left on the wire. This is the whole transition implementation hass-ddp needs: it knows both colors, aioddp knows nothing about state.

Fading between two effects is out of scope. hass-ddp stops the old runner, fades to the new solid color if any, and starts the new runner.
path: aioddp component spec: EffectRunner and fades

items.title: Tests (tests/test_runner.py)
items.text:
• Start a breathe runner at 50 fps against the UDP listener for 0.2 s: between 8 and 12 frames received, offsets equal the segment's byte offset, every packet has push set
  • Static palette runner: exactly one frame sent, running false afterwards, wait() returns, no task left in asyncio.all_tasks()
  • stop() while running: no task left, stop() again is a no-op, error is None
  • update(params=...) changes the next frame's bytes (chase with a new color); bad params raise EffectError and leave the old ones in place
  • update(fps=...) changes the frame rate (count frames over a window)
  • Render that raises: inject an effect class whose render raises; task ends, error set, wait() re-raises, no task left
  • Sender closed during run: loop ends with DDPSendError in error
  • Falling behind: effect whose render sleeps synchronously 50 ms at 30 fps for 0.3 s; frames_dropped > 0 and the task still exits cleanly on stop()
  • fade: 10 frames at duration=1, fps=10, first frame is near start, last frame is exactly end after the color pipeline, duration=0 sends one frame
  • Budget guard: max_render_seconds is populated

items.title: aioddp component spec: DDPSender
items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Module: sender.py

items.title: Scope
items.text: The one object that owns a socket. Everything that reaches the controller goes through DDPSender.send_frame, which runs the color pipeline and so cannot bypass the brightness cap. Async only; the sync wrapper is deferred (see the end).

items.title: Construction and lifecycle
items.text:
class DDPSender:
    def __init__(
        self,
        strip: Strip,
        *,
        keepalive_interval: float | None = None,
        bind_host: str | None = None,
    ) -> None

    async def open(self) -> None
    async def close(self) -> None
    async def __aenter__(self) -> DDPSender      # open()
    async def __aexit__(...) -> None             # close()

    @property
    def is_open(self) -> bool
    @property
    def strip(self) -> Strip
    @property
    def stats(self) -> SenderStats
  • open() calls loop.create_datagram_endpoint(_DDPProtocol, remote_addr=(strip.host, strip.port), local_addr=(bind_host, 0) if bind_host else None). Name resolution happens here. OSError (unresolvable host, no route, bind failure) is re-raised as DDPSendError with the original as __cause__. Opening an already open sender is a no-op
  • close() cancels the keepalive task, awaits it, closes the transport, and sets is_open false. Idempotent. It does not blank the lights; a reload must not flash the house
  • The sender is bound to the event loop it was opened on and is not thread-safe. Nothing in it uses threads or executors
  • keepalive_interval must be None or >= 0.5 seconds, else ConfigError

items.title: Sending
items.text:
async def send_frame(
        self,
        pixels: bytes,
        *,
        segment: Segment | None = None,
        brightness: float = 1.0,
        push: bool = True,
    ) -> None

    async def fill(self, segment: Segment | None, color: Color, *, brightness: float = 1.0, push: bool = True) -> None
    async def off(self, segment: Segment | None = None, *, push: bool = True) -> None
    async def push(self) -> None

send_frame:

  1. Raise DDPSendError if not open
  2. Resolve the target: segment or strip.full_segment(); strip.validate_segment it
  3. Require len(pixels) == strip.byte_length(segment); if the strip is RGBW and len(pixels) equals segment.length * 3, expand with expand_rgb_to_rgbw first. Any other length is ConfigError
  4. wire = process_frame(pixels, strip, brightness=brightness, reverse=segment.reverse)
  5. Copy wire into the shadow buffer at strip.byte_offset(segment)
  6. packets = build_packets(wire, base_offset=..., data_type=strip.wire_data_type, sequence=self._seq, push=push, destination=strip.destination_id)
  7. transport.sendto(p) for each packet, with no await between packets so two coroutines sending concurrently cannot interleave the packets of one frame
  8. Update stats and last_send

fill is send_frame(solid_pixels(color, segment.length, strip.channels), ...). off is fill with black at brightness 1.0, and it is the only thing that blanks a strip. push sends build_push_packet; use it after a series of push=False sends to latch them together on receivers that honor a zero-length push.

Declared async even though sendto does not await, so the API does not change if pacing is added and so hass-ddp's call sites are uniform.

items.title: Querying
items.text:
async def query(self, destination: int = DESTINATION_CONFIG, *, timeout: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, Any] | None

The one read path. Sends build_query_packet and waits up to timeout for reply packets (reply flag set, matching destination) until one carries push; returns the parsed JSON object, None on timeout or an empty reply, DDPQueryError on an unparseable one. _DDPProtocol.datagram_received exists only to feed this; every other datagram is dropped. Full contract, including concurrency and close behavior, is in 2026-10-29-aioddp-discovery.md.

items.title: Shadow buffer
items.text:
self._shadow = bytearray(strip.frame_size) holds the last wire bytes sent for every position, initially all zero. Three things read it:

  • Keepalive resends it whole
  • stats.last_frame exposes a bytes copy for diagnostics and tests
  • Nothing else. It is not a source of truth for color, since it is post-pipeline; hass-ddp keeps its own state

items.title: Keepalive
items.text:
When keepalive_interval is set, open() starts one task:

loop:
    sleep(interval)
    if now - last_send >= interval and any frame has been sent:
        send the shadow buffer as one full-strip frame, push=True, via build_packets

It reuses the sequence counter and counts in stats like any other send. It runs only when the caller has been idle, so an active effect never doubles traffic. It is off by default; the compatibility page records which controllers blank without it. The task is created with a name (aioddp-keepalive-<host>) and close() always cancels and awaits it so no task outlives the sender.

items.title: release()
items.text:
def release(self) -> None

Pauses keepalive resends until the next send_frame (and so fill or off), which resumes them. It is synchronous because it only sets a flag: it sends nothing, does not close the socket, and does not cancel the keepalive task, which keeps ticking and skips while released. Without keepalive, or on a closed sender, it is a harmless no-op. This exists for controllers with built-in effects: DDP data overrides the built-in effect, and the controller falls back to it some time after DDP stops (about 20 s on the controller recorded in docs/compatibility.md), so handing the lights back to the controller means no more DDP, keepalive included. push() does not resume keepalive; it latches, it is not a frame.

items.title: Error handling
items.text:
• _DDPProtocol.error_received(exc) logs at WARNING once per distinct errno and then at DEBUG, increments stats.send_errors. ICMP port-unreachable on a controller that is off shows up here; it must not kill an effect loop
  • _DDPProtocol.connection_lost(exc) marks the sender closed and logs at WARNING if exc is not None. The next send_frame raises DDPSendError
  • transport.sendto itself does not raise for UDP; if it ever does, the OSError is caught, counted, and logged, not raised
  • Frames are never logged above DEBUG, and at DEBUG only the header fields and byte length, never the payload

items.title: SenderStats
items.text:
@dataclass(slots=True)
class SenderStats:
    packets_sent: int = 0
    bytes_sent: int = 0
    frames_sent: int = 0
    keepalives_sent: int = 0
    send_errors: int = 0
    replies_received: int = 0  # completed query replies
    last_send: float | None = None  # loop.time()
    last_frame: bytes = b""  # copy of the shadow buffer at last send

stats returns the live object; hass-ddp diagnostics read it. It is not reset by close().

items.title: Concurrency contract
items.text:
• One DDPSender per controller. Two senders to one host fight at the controller and the library does not detect it
  • Any number of coroutines may call send_frame concurrently; each frame's packets are contiguous on the wire because there is no suspension point inside the send loop
  • Rate limiting is not implemented. At 30 fps a 1000-pixel RGB strip is 90 packets per second, which is nothing. If a controller needs pacing, that is a compatibility-page note and a later feature

items.title: Tests (tests/test_sender.py)
items.text:
All against the udp_listener fixture from the testing spec; no mocking of asyncio.

  • fill on full strip: one packet, header matches golden, payload is the capped and reordered bytes
  • fill on a segment at pixel 100 of an RGB strip: offset 300
  • Frame larger than 1440 bytes: packet count, offsets, push only on last, sequence numbers consecutive
  • RGB pixels sent to an RGBW strip are expanded; wrong length raises ConfigError
  • Two segments sent with push=False then push(): three sends, push bit only on the latch packet
  • off writes zeros into the shadow buffer and onto the wire
  • Keepalive at 0.5 s with a fake clock or short real sleep: no packets while sending every 0.1 s; one full-strip resend after idle
  • close() cancels keepalive (no pending tasks after, asserted via asyncio.all_tasks), second close() is a no-op, send_frame after close raises DDPSendError
  • Unresolvable host raises DDPSendError from open()
  • error_received increments send_errors and does not raise
  • query: the listener fixture's responder hook answers; full, split, empty, malformed, and absent replies, plus close while pending (cases listed in the discovery spec)

items.title: Deferred: sync wrapper
items.text: sender_sync.py is not in 0.1.0. The CLI covers scripting, and a sync API would need its own loop-ownership rules that the keepalive task makes awkward. If a demand appears, the shape is DDPSenderSync(strip) running a private loop in asyncio.run-style for each call, with no keepalive. The design doc's open question stays open until then; this spec's recommendation is to drop it.

items.text: Date: 2026-10-28 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Module: strip.py

items.title: Scope
items.text: Immutable configuration models. Everything else in the library takes a Strip and zero or more Segments and never re-validates what these classes already guarantee. No I/O.
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Strip
items.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Strip:
    host: str
    pixel_count: int
    port: int = DDP_PORT
    data_type: DataType = DataType.RGB
    color_order: str = ""  # empty: the data type's canonical order, RGB or RGBW
    brightness_cap: float = DEFAULT_BRIGHTNESS_CAP
    gamma: float | None = DEFAULT_GAMMA
    destination_id: int = DESTINATION_DEFAULT
    data_type_byte: int | None = None
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Validation (__post_init__, raises ConfigError)
items.text:
Field Rule host Non-empty after strip(). Not resolved here; resolution happens when the sender opens pixel_count Integer, 1 <= pixel_count <= MAX_OFFSET // channels. In practice the upper bound is never reached port 1 to 65535 data_type A DataType member. Strings are not coerced here; the CLI and hass-ddp map user input to the enum color_order Empty (the default) means the canonical order for the data type. Otherwise upper-cased and must be a permutation of "RGB" for DataType.RGB and of "RGBW" for DataType.RGBW. "GRB", "BRG", "GRBW" are all valid; "RGB" on an RGBW strip is an error, as is a repeated letter brightness_cap 0.0 < cap <= 1.0. Zero is rejected because it makes every frame black and is never what a user meant gamma None or 1.0 disables correction; otherwise 1.0 < gamma <= 4.0 destination_id 0 to 255 data_type_byte None or 0 to 255

Validation normalizes color_order to upper case; because the dataclass is frozen this is done with object.__setattr__ in __post_init__.
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Derived properties
items.text:
channels: int  # data_type.channels
frame_size: int  # pixel_count * channels, in bytes
wire_data_type: int  # data_type_byte if set, else data_type.wire_byte
channel_map: tuple[int, ...]  # for each output channel position, the canonical index to read from

channel_map for "GRB" is (1, 0, 2): output position 0 reads canonical channel 1 (G). The color pipeline uses it directly.
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Segment helpers
items.text:
def full_segment(self, name: str = "all") -> Segment
def validate_segment(self, segment: Segment) -> None     # raises ConfigError when out of range
def byte_offset(self, segment: Segment) -> int           # segment.start * channels
def byte_length(self, segment: Segment) -> int           # segment.length * channels
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Segment
items.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class Segment:
    name: str
    start: int
    length: int
    reverse: bool = False

    @property
    def end(self) -> int      # exclusive: start + length
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Validation (__post_init__, raises ConfigError)
items.text:
• name non-empty after strip(); stored stripped. No slug rules; hass-ddp slugifies for entity IDs
  • start >= 0
  • length >= 1

A Segment does not know its strip, so range checking happens in Strip.validate_segment, called by the sender on every fill, off, and send_frame. It is a two-comparison check and is not cached. Overlap between segments is allowed: the library does not own a segment list, hass-ddp does, and it enforces non-overlap in its options flow because overlapping entities would fight.
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: reverse
items.text: reverse=True means pixel index 0 of the rendered frame lands on the last physical pixel of the segment. It is applied as the final step of the color pipeline (see the color spec) and never changes start or length. A reversed segment still has one byte offset: start * channels.
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: Usage
items.text:
strip = Strip(host="10.0.40.20", pixel_count=300, color_order="GRB", brightness_cap=0.6)
roof = Segment("roofline", start=0, length=260)
peak = Segment("peak", start=260, length=40, reverse=True)
strip.validate_segment(peak)  # ok
Segment("bad", start=290, length=20)  # ConfigError from validate_segment: ends at 310 > 300
path: aioddp component spec: Strip and Segment

items.title: udp_listener
items.text:
class UDPListener:
    host: str                # "127.0.0.1"
    port: int                # ephemeral, bound at fixture setup
    packets: list[bytes]     # raw datagrams in arrival order
    async def wait_for(self, count: int, timeout: float = 1.0) -> list[bytes]
    def headers(self) -> list[DDPHeader]
    def payloads(self) -> list[bytes]
    def clear(self) -> None

An asyncio DatagramProtocol bound on loopback. Every sender and CLI test points a Strip at listener.host/listener.port, so tests assert real bytes on a real socket with no mocking of asyncio. An optional responder callable ((data, addr) -> list[bytes]) sends datagrams back to the sender, which is how query replies are tested. The captured config and status documents (CONFIG_JSON, STATUS_JSON) and config_responder serve query replies. wait_for polls on a short sleep rather than using a condition so the loop keeps running the sender's tasks. Loopback never drops datagrams at this volume; if a test sees fewer packets than expected it is a real bug, not flakiness.

items.title: Benchmark gate (tests/test_effects.py::test_render_budget)

items.text:
Not automated. Run before 0.1.0 and record the answers in docs/compatibility.md:

items.title: aioddp component spec: query and discovery
items.text: Date: 2026-10-29 Status: Draft Parent: 2026-10-28-aioddp-design.md Modules: discovery.py, plus DDPSender.query in sender.py and build_query_packet in protocol.py
path: aioddp component spec: query and discovery

items.title: Scope
items.text:
DDP has no handshake, so a sender cannot learn a controller's pixel count or output layout from the data path. The protocol has an optional read side: a packet with the query flag to destination 250 (JSON config) or 251 (JSON status) gets a reply carrying a JSON document. This spec adds that query to the sender, and a parser for the config document. The result is a ControllerLayout that hass-ddp can turn into a Strip and one Segment per output.

Discovery is best effort. Nothing in the data path depends on it, and a controller that answers nothing is configured by hand exactly as before.

aioddp has no HTTP client and knows no vendor. Some controllers (the Minleon NDB-Pro) publish the same config document over HTTP instead of answering UDP queries; the separate pyminleon library fetches it and hands the JSON to parse_config, which is public for that reason. Nothing here depends on pyminleon.
path: aioddp component spec: query and discovery

items.title: The config document
items.text:
From the DDP spec ("schema as used in Minleon NDB", the one place a vendor is named, because the extensions below come from it):

{"config": {"ip": "a.b.c.d", "nm": "a.b.c.d", "gw": "a.b.c.d",
            "ports": [{"port": 0, "ts": 0, "l": 80, "ss": 1}, ...]}}

Per port: l is the number of lights (pixels), ss the 1-based starting slot (channel) in the controller's flat buffer. Controllers may add p as an alias for port, rev (the controller reverses that output itself), proto (0 DDP, 1 Art-Net, 2 E1.31), and conv, the input-to-pixel conversion whose input channel count is:

conv Input channels conv Input channels 0, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 12, 13 3 2, 8, 14 4 3, 9 1 (white only; aioddp cannot drive it)

Pixel start of an output is (ss - 1) // channels. The buffer is one flat buffer across outputs, for example output 2 at slot 241 is pixel 80 when output 1 has 80 three-channel pixels.

The status document is {"status": {"man": ..., "mod": ..., "ver": ..., ...}}; only those three keys are interpreted.
path: aioddp component spec: query and discovery

items.title: protocol.py additions
items.text:
DESTINATION_CONTROL = 246   # const.py
DESTINATION_CONFIG = 250
DESTINATION_STATUS = 251

class DDPHeader:
    @property
    def query(self) -> bool     # FLAG_QUERY
    @property
    def reply(self) -> bool     # FLAG_REPLY

def build_query_packet(*, sequence: SequenceCounter, destination: int, offset: int = 0, length: int = 0) -> bytes

A header-only packet: flags FLAG_VERSION_1 | FLAG_QUERY, data type 0, validated like build_header, one sequence number consumed. Golden vectors: destination 250 at sequence 1 is 42 01 00 FA 00000000 0000; destination 251 at sequence 2 is 42 02 00 FB 00000000 0000.
path: aioddp component spec: query and discovery

items.title: DDPSender.query
items.text:
async def query(self, destination: int = DESTINATION_CONFIG, *, timeout: float = 1.0) -> dict[str, Any] | None
  • Raises DDPSendError when the sender is not open and ConfigError for a timeout that is not a positive finite number
  • Sends one query packet through the normal send path (it counts in stats.packets_sent and prints the DEBUG line)
  • Waits up to timeout for a reply: datagrams with the reply flag and a matching destination are collected, data[10:10 + length] per packet, keyed by header offset (a repeated offset replaces), until one arrives with push set, which per the spec marks the end of the reply. The chunks must then be contiguous from offset 0, else the query raises DDPQueryError naming the gap. Anything else received on the socket is ignored
  • Replies are matched by destination only, because the spec does not say a reply echoes the query's sequence number. A reply that arrives after its query timed out is dropped, unless a new query to the same destination is already pending, in which case that query returns it. In practice a query is one round trip and discover makes one per destination, so this is noted, not guarded
  • Returns None on timeout or on an empty reply (the spec's "reading not supported" answer is length 0 with push). Returns the parsed JSON object otherwise. A reply that is not valid JSON or not an object raises DDPQueryError
  • One pending query per destination; a second concurrent query to the same destination is a programmer error (RuntimeError). Queries to different destinations may overlap
  • close() or a lost connection fails a pending query with DDPSendError; nothing hangs and no task leaks
  • stats.replies_received counts completed replies
  • _DDPProtocol.datagram_received is the only receive path in the library. It feeds query and nothing else; aioddp is still not a DDP receiver

DDPQueryError(DDPError) is new: a controller answered a query or config request with something unusable.
path: aioddp component spec: query and discovery

items.title: discovery.py
items.text:
@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class OutputInfo:
    index: int                      # controller output number as reported, 0-based
    start: int                      # first pixel in the flat buffer, 0-based
    length: int                     # pixels; 0 means unused
    reversed_by_controller: bool = False

@dataclass(frozen=True, slots=True)
class ControllerLayout:
    host: str
    source: str                     # "ddp" for the UDP query; for parse_config, whatever the caller passes
    pixel_count: int                # max(start + length) over active outputs, else 0
    channels: int                   # channels per input pixel used for slot math
    outputs: tuple[OutputInfo, ...]
    protocol: str | None            # "ddp", "artnet", "e131", or None when the document does not say
    manufacturer: str | None
    model: str | None
    firmware: str | None
    config: Mapping[str, Any]       # the inner config object as received
    status: Mapping[str, Any] | None

    @property
    def active_outputs(self) -> tuple[OutputInfo, ...]
    @property
    def data_type(self) -> DataType | None     # RGB for 3 channels, RGBW for 4, else None
    def segments(self) -> list[Segment]        # one per active output

items.title: parse_config
items.text:
Accepts the {"config": {...}} wrapper or the inner object, and the same for status. ports must be a list of mappings with integer l >= 0 and ss >= 1 (decimal strings accepted, since the spec's example is loose about types); anything else, a duplicate port index, a rev that is not a bool or int, or an output that would end past MAX_OFFSET is DDPQueryError naming the port. A document from the DDP query was decoded by decode_json_document, which rejects NaN and Infinity; a caller passing its own document is responsible for decoding it the same way. channels comes from conv when present and known, else is inferred from the first two active outputs when ss2 - ss1 == l1 * c for c in 3 or 4, else defaults to 3. (ss - 1) must divide by channels.

segments() returns Segment(f"output{index + 1}", start, length) for each active output, named to match the controller's 1-based "Output 1" in its web UI. reverse is always False: when the controller reverses an output itself, the pixel order in the DDP buffer is already what the controller wants, and reversing again in aioddp would undo it. reversed_by_controller carries the fact for display.

items.text: Opens a throwaway DDPSender on Strip(host, pixel_count=1, port=port), queries config, then status as a best-effort second query, closes the sender whether or not anything answered. None when config does not answer. DDPSendError from opening the socket propagates.

items.title: CLI: aioddp query
items.text:
aioddp --host HOST query [--timeout 1.0] [--json]

Needs host and port only; --count is what this command exists to find. Human output is the controller identity line (when status answered), one row per active output with pixels, start, and whether the controller reverses it, a count of unused outputs, the total, and a config.yaml snippet with strip and one segment per active output, ready to paste. A protocol other than DDP or a channel count aioddp cannot drive prints a warning on stderr. --json prints one object with host, source, manufacturer, model, firmware, protocol, pixel_count, channels, data_type, outputs, and the raw config and status documents.

No answer exits 2 with a message naming the host and the DDP port. A malformed answer exits 1 through the normal DDPError mapping.

items.title: Compatibility notes
items.text: The Minleon NDB-Pro (firmware 2.0) does not answer UDP queries to 250 or 251, from either an ephemeral source port or port 4048, so aioddp query gets no answer from it; its HTTP-served documents are read by pyminleon. Its status document reports "push": true. Both facts are recorded in docs/compatibility.md.
